title: aws-node must carry ENABLE_IPv4 (v1.10+) — an image-only bump crash-loops ipamd

detection.reason: the rule asks whether an env var is ABSENT from the aws-node container; the detection vocabulary can only test presence, so the hint names the DaemonSet and the command checks the name

quote: cni v1.10.x introduced 2 new env variables - ENABLE_IPv4 and ENABLE_IPv6. The above error can be caused if you miss adding these env variables to your cni daemonset.
remediation: Upgrade by applying the full release manifest (or the EKS add-on / chart), not by editing the image tag on the existing DaemonSet. From v1.10 ipamd's code default for ENABLE_IPv4 is false (ENABLE_IPv6 absent simply means false), so an aws-node container without ENABLE_IPv4=true runs with both families off: v1.10 panicked in StartNodeIPPoolManager, and through v1.23 ipamd exits on validation ("IPv4 and IPv6 are both disabled"). Either way the DaemonSet crash-loops and every new pod waits for an IP.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get ds aws-node -o json | jq -r '[.spec.template.spec.containers[] | select(.name == "aws-node") | .env[]?.name] as $e | if ($e | index("ENABLE_IPv4")) then "ok: ENABLE_IPv4 set" else "MISSING: ENABLE_IPv4" end'  # MISSING = ipamd starts with both address families disabled and exits; apply the release manifest instead of only bumping the image
coversNotes: ENABLE_IPv4 (v1.10.0+) Type: Boolean as a String Default: true VPC CNI can operate in
ENABLE_IPv6 (v1.10.0+) Type: Boolean as a String Default: false VPC CNI can operate in
